messages.subject: Possible memory leak?
parts:
Hello all,

I am trying to fit a Stan model which links a set of pixel-values to behavior on some binomial trials. The model compiles without problems, and when run with a very small pixel-matrix, the sampling works correctly. However, this is for pixel-matrices which are way too small to be meaningful for my analysis, and when I scale it up a bit, sampling will start, but will break at some point with a std::bad_alloc error. While sampling is occuring I can see the memory use of my computer skyrocket, and it keeps rising as I iterate through the trials I am fitting. Additionally, after the std::bad_alloc error, the memory use stays high untill I close the R-session in which Stan is running.

Attached you can find the model.txt and the data-dump of the variable passed to the model. Here follows some technical information on my setup:

Running Stan via R in ESS (Emacs)
Reproduced the same error when running as an R-script from the commandline (without Emacs)
Running on Arch-Linux 64bit

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible memory leak?
parts:
Are you using the 1.3 release version of Stan?

We don't know of any memory leaks in any of our versions
related to anything you're doing.

I tried it using 1.3 command line to reduce the number
of moving parts and it allocated 9.3GB up front,
but didn't continue to allocate memory after that. It
may look gradual to you if you don't have 16GB of
free memory.

I'm not clear from looking at the model or it's 2MB
data file why the memory usage would be so high! So
I added a transformed data block with a print statement
to signal when the data init's complete, and the memory's
well under 1GB at the point the data's read in.

So I'm guessing it's an issue with the expression graph,
which is created in every evaluation of the model.
It builds out every operation in memory that's applied
to compute the log probability. These can add up.

So if Nmes * Npix is big, you're in trouble. Every intermediate
expression used in that inner loop is saved as part
of the expression graph generated for automatic differentiation.

It does not appear to be a leak in that the memory
stays constant after the 9.3GB first loop.

The best way to trim them down is to share computations.
Things like not computing (kappa+eta) multiple times
or pow(gamma,kappa) multiple times. This will also make
the code much faster. It counterintuitively uses less
memory to write variables into a local variable array or
vector, then apply the sum() operation to them. It's
also much faster.

Also, looking at the model, it's odd to me to see
something that looks almost, but not quite, like
logistic regression. Usually you see 1/(1 + exp(-alpha)).
If you can convert to that form, you can use binomial_logit(Ntot,alpha)
instead of the above. That will also save you memory and
time. (Though binomial_logit may not be out until Stan 2.0;
I can't recall if it was in 1.3.)

Starting with --init=0, it takes about 120s for 20 iterations
on my notebook. But it didn't get anywhere; I'm trying a longer
run.

In general, I'd suggest starting with a smaller model or
less data in the same model, to make sure the model's fitting
properly.

- Bob

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Possible memory leak?
parts:
The model's problematic in that the autodif
values are all nan. This is indicative of another
problem.

~/temp2/janssen$ ./janssen --test_grad --data=dat_breaks.data.R
done

TEST GRADIENT MODE

Log probability=-9081.1

param idx value model finite diff error
0 1.72463 nan -0.69745 nan
1 1.80643 nan -0.71786 nan
2 -0.828554 nan 0.392099 nan
3 0.692461 nan -0.333029 nan

I'm not sure what the issue is there, but you might
want to debug by creating simpler models if possible.

This is probably some kind of auto-diff issue, so I'm
going to create an issue for us to track the it:

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/216

We might not get back to it until after 2.0 is out, because
we're totally swamped trying to get that out. This is probably
an issue somewhere in the model. If you figure it out, please
let us know on this list or by commenting on the issue.

Also, for memory, you really want to move statements like
this

msk_pix <- pix[p] * msk_c[m];

that only involved data out of inner loops in the model.
You're better off with a transformed data block declaring
msk_pix to a matrix (or 2D array, though matrices are faster
for 2D access) and setting msk_pix[p,m] in the transformed
data block. Data only uses double
values for numbers (8 bytes/number) and will be at least
an order of magnitude faster to compute.

- Bob

messages.author: 6b4344ac0a816534
messages.subject: Re: Possible memory leak?
parts:
Hey Bob,

Thanks for the feedback!

First of all: Yep, version 1.3

It is quite counter-intuitive that storing things in a local vector would reduce the memory overhead. I had actually coded it like that in my first version, but removed this structure to conserve on memory. I will definitely change that.

Also, of course computing the pow(gamma, kappa) and (kappa + eta) will help out, thanks for the heads up.

Additionally, the 'slightly-off' logistic regression form comes from the fact that I am currently trying to reproduce the model of the person who came before me, but who was running the models in a homebrewed but underperforming MCMC algorithm. That way I was hoping to get an almost exact duplication of results before moving on to tweaking and finessing the model itself. But perhaps I should perform these tweaks right now. I can always transform the parameters I recover back into the parameters fit by that model.

Perhaps the fact that I am only running 8GB of RAM on this machine is a problem. Perhaps its time to upgrade.

It is now almost 21.00 here. I'll make the changes and keep you up to date tomorrow morning.

David
